thread:
oliver: quick check — thinking about letting us oversubscribe private-endpoint shards per-region to cut dedicated cp node count. idea: advertise shard-level routes and use ephemeral pinning for request affinity. main concerns: conntrack and SNAT pressure when a shard gets a traffic spike. thoughts?
maria: do you mean one cp shard handles multiple customer endpoints in the same AZ? how would TLS termination and certs work? :thinking_face:
oliver: yes — shard = group of endpoints that own a routable IP in the tenant subnet. TLS stays end-to-end (SNI passthrough), cp only forwards / proxies. we avoid terminating customer certs on our side where possible.
srini: big red flag: if we're SNATing egress to a shard IP we'll quickly blow conntrack. we hit this in staging when 3 shards per AZ handled unexpected load — conntrack exhaustion in ~4h. need per-tenant SNAT pools or source preservation strategy.
jess: also ops-wise latency will vary a lot under oversubscribe. p50 ok but p99 spikes. recommend circuit breakers at routing layer + token-bucket per-shard to protect tail latency.
max: implementation notes: options i see — (1) ENI-per-shard and advertise /32s from VPC route table (avoids SNAT), (2) shared proxy with connection reuse and aggressive keepalives, (3) per-tenant SNAT pools. ENI approach reduces NAT but runs into ENI limits at scale.
srini: exactly — ENI per-shard won't scale across many accounts/instances. we hit ENI limits if we go that route for 100s of shards. not viable long-term.
maria: what about ephemeral pinning? handshake goes to CP control plane, CP returns backend IP and we pin the client to that backend for pin_ttl (e.g., 2m). reduces routing churn and conntrack load per-request.
oliver: i like ephemeral pinning + health-aware oversubscribe. propose we maintain a max oversubscribe ratio (e.g., 3:1) per shard and slow-start tenants onto an oversubscribed shard. if metrics degrade, evict to dedicated shard.
jess: metrics we should track: per-shard conntrack_util, avg_conn_per_src, cpu, active_streams, keepalive_reuse_rate. alerts if tail latency > 2x baseline or conntrack_util > 70%.
max: config sketch (will open PR):
```
shard_config:
  oversubscribe_ratio: 3
  snat_policy: per_tenant_pool
  pin_ttl_seconds: 120
  cb_threshold_rtt_ms: 500
```
this gives ops knobs and a clear rollback path.
oliver: rollout questions — prefer canary in staging, then us-east-1, then AZ-by-AZ. also need migration playbook to move endpoints off overloaded shards.
srini: playbook notes: immediate mitigation = move route to fallback shard or dedicated shard, drain conntrack (conntrack -D --orig-src <ip> or restart nat path), and scale up shard if eviction causes ripple. run a pre-migration scale test to estimate drain time.
deploy-bot: deploy status: cp-agent v2.4.0 -> canary in us-east-1 started :rocket:
maria: action items: oliver to write RFC with diagrams + capacity model; max to open PR with shard_config defaults; jess to define dashboards & alerts; srini to run conntrack + load test and report thresholds.
oliver: will do. thanks team :thumbsup:
